summary:
==============================
Case 033
==============================

1. Patient Context
- Age 63, female; community optometry practice setting
- Falls pathway: routine eye examination where mobility-related blur was identified; no confirmed fall, but patient reports hesitancy on uneven paving when walking without glasses
- Chief complaint: “I take my glasses off to read and then forget to put them back on”
- Vision history and status: longstanding low myopia with progressive distance blur when mobile; uses single-vision distance spectacles only and no dedicated reading correction; habitually removes spectacles for near tasks and then walks around unaided
- Functional implications from findings: distance blur improves with correction; near tasks require reading correction; outdoors, misjudging garden path edges and slowing in dull weather noted
- Driving: drives regularly and avoids driving without glasses; license requires glasses
- Ocular health: early nuclear sclerosis OU; mild meibomian gland dysfunction OU; full visual fields; binocular alignment orthophoric distance with near exophoria tendency; stereo acuity not optimal; full motility; no diplopia; contrast sensitivity within normal limits
- Management plan from optometry: updated distance and near prescriptions; introduction of first-time multifocals with adaptation support and fall-risk awareness; advised consistent distance correction when walking indoors/outdoors; distance correction required for driving license; follow-up in 6 weeks to assess adaptation and mobility confidence

2. Key Vision Issues
- Distance blur when mobile due to under-correction, contributing to uncertain obstacle and edge detection outdoors (e.g., garden path edges) and slower outdoor pace, particularly in dull lighting
- Habitual removal of glasses for near tasks creates a period of distance blur during ambulation, increasing risk for misjudging surfaces or steps
- Near-vision correction pending/advised with multifocals; adaptation period may temporarily affect safe mobility and task performance during the transition
- Binocular alignment near shows a mild exophoric tendency with suboptimal depth perception; may contribute to shallow depth cues when edges or surface boundaries are uncertain
- Early nuclear sclerosis and mild ocular surface changes may exacerbate blur or glare in low-contrast, low-light conditions though overall contrast sensitivity is normal

3. Functional Impact
Mobility and Falls
- Outdoor ambulation on uneven surfaces (e.g., garden paths) may be less safe when distance vision is uncorrected or during adaptation to new correction; dull lighting may further reduce edge/step visibility and increase hesitancy
ADLs/IADLs
- Reading and near tasks currently rely on removing glasses; risk that habitual non-wear during mobility leads to inconsistent vision during tasks such as reading labels or forms while moving, or reading near items in unfamiliar environments
Participation / Confidence / Roles
- Reported hesitancy outdoors and need to slow down in certain conditions may reduce outdoor activity and confidence; driving safety relies on wearing distance correction
Environmental Interaction
- Poor lighting/dull weather reduces contrast and edge delineation, interacting with underlying under-correction and mild binocular/depth-perception factors

4. Vision-Informed OT Considerations
Self-care
- Assess whether reading small print or labels (e.g., medication labels) is affected when not wearing reading correction; consider whether near tasks can be reliably completed with the recommended near add
Mobility Strategies
- Given distance blur outdoors and near exophoria, consider a referral to Orientation & Mobility (O&M) for mobility assessment and strategy development, particularly for navigating uneven pavements and low-contrast surfaces; avoid prescriptive routines here, but outline potential goals (e.g., improved route safety, safer edge detection, and transfer of scanning strategies)
Environmental Modifications / Home Environment
- Consider broader outdoor environmental assessment and potential modifications to support safer ambulation (e.g., well-lit, even walking routes; contrast-enhancing cues on edges); within the home, ensure clear pathways and consistent footwear or footwear-adapted strategies for when vision shifts during tasks
Lighting and Contrast
- Assess habitual lighting conditions encountered outdoors (glare, shadowing, low contrast) and indoors (entryways, stairs) to guide recommendations for task lighting and environmental contrast adjustments; avoid assuming “brighter is always better” and tailor to her functional needs
Task Adaptations
- Emphasize strategies to support wearing corrective lenses consistently during ambulation (e.g., memory cues, placement by doorways, routines linking glasses with shoes/coats); consider near tasks performed while stationary to minimize dual-task risk
Assistive Technology / Non-visual Strategies
- If adaptation to multifocals is challenging, discuss non-visual compensation strategies (e.g., tactile cues for stairs, landmark-based navigation) and ensure ongoing eye-care guidance remains primary
Education and Support
- Educate on the importance of consistent distance correction for mobility and driving; provide practical tips to support adherence during transitions to multifocals; address the risk of forgetting to wear glasses
Clinical Follow-up / Communication
- Align follow-up with optometry plan (6 weeks) and be prepared to liaise with optometry if glare, edge detection or depth-perception concerns persist; consider O&M referral if mobility safety remains suboptimal after adaptation
Driving / Transport
- Reinforce that distance correction is required for driving; support planning for ongoing use of glasses during driving and potential pursuit of a driving-related refresher or assessment if concerns arise
Information gaps to clarify (for OT planning)
- Any current or planned use of reading glasses in daily activities beyond the near add
- Specific outdoor routes where hesitancy or near-miss incidents occur to target assessment
- Availability of support during transitions to multifocals (e.g., supervision, home environment changes)

Falls Risk Level
- Moderate
- Rationale: observable hesitation and misjudgment on uneven surfaces when glasses are not worn, combined with ongoing adaptation to new lens correction and mild binocular depth cues, poses a tangible but not definitive mobility risk; no documented falls, but near-miss potential is present

5. Summary of Key OT Considerations from Vision Findings
- Ensure alignment between updated prescriptions, sunglasses/eyewear use, and consistent spectacle wear during ambulation to reduce distance blur and edge misperception in outdoor environments
- Consider referral to Orientation & Mobility to address safe navigation on uneven surfaces, particularly in low-contrast lighting; support goals may include improved edge detection and confidence during outdoor walks
- Assess and plan for near-vision task performance during movement (e.g., reading while standing vs. walking) and medication label reading; ensure near correction is accessible and used as needed
- Provide or plan education around habit formation to wear distance correction for mobility and driving; include practical cues and routines to minimize forgetfulness
- Evaluate environmental factors in common outdoor routes (lighting, contrast, clutter) and consider recommendations to optimize safety without assuming fixed environmental changes; incorporate patient preferences and feasibility
- Schedule follow-up in 6 weeks to monitor adaptation to new correction and mobility confidence; escalate to O&M or additional vision-support services if mobility risk remains or increases

Notes
- All recommendations are contingent on case-specific information and aim to support functional safety and independence without replacing optometric management
- This summary focuses on translating vision findings into OT-relevant functional implications and potential avenues for OT assessment and collaboration with eye care providers
